G1.name: Requirements
G1.note: Owner approval: M12 requirements Revision 4, including FR-32, are approved. The original manifest's complete resolved dependency set is the comparison baseline; introduced packages are reported only when both original and proposed resolutions are COMPATIBLE. The comparison is informational and does not add an approval gate. Upload dates must be verified against the exact selected distribution file. Compatibility is not a security endorsement. OSV and malware detection remain outside M12.

G2.name: Architecture and threat model
G2.note: Owner approval: M12 architecture Revision 4, ADR-009 through ADR-012, and the revised threat model are approved. T-35 is accepted at High inherent severity and Medium residual risk, with FR-32 compatibility disclosures and resolved-set review. COMPATIBLE means dependency resolution success, not package safety. Resolution failures must use trusted supervisor-generated evidence only. Unsupported configurations remain fail-closed. Docker isolation and network controls remain unverified until the required live integration tests pass.

G3.name: Milestone plan
G3.note: Owner approval: M12 construction is authorized against the approved requirements Revision 4, architecture Revision 4, threat model Revision 4, ADR-009 through ADR-012, and the registered 14 acceptance criteria. T-35 residual risk is accepted at Medium as approved at G2. CI work-in-progress pushes to the existing feature branch are authorized using normal pushes only. Test-only resolver fixtures are authorized provided they exercise the real supervisor verification and fingerprinting path. No security assertions may be weakened, deleted or skipped. M12 must demonstrate live Docker isolation and resolver integration in CI before relevant criteria are accepted.

G5.name: Release
G5.note: New intent (Inception round 2 / one-day sprint). Owner authorized: 'After the governance checkpoint is committed, proceed with the authorized G1 reset and requirements Revision 2 preparation.' and 'Keep the existing AI-DLC approval requirements. Compress governance preparation and approvals into the minimum necessary process.'

criteria.proof: repository_service: strict URL parser, global-IP resolution check, api.github.com pre-check (exists/public/size, same-host redirects only), hardened git flags + empty env, RLIMIT_FSIZE + 250 ms watchdog + timeout, discovery with exclusions/depth/size caps; live clone of pallets/itsdangerous, microblog, expressjs/cors; 45 tests.

criteria.text: Server-authoritative RunStore and server-recorded approval; validation, apply and export return 409 without approval (FR-15/FR-16)

criteria.text: Host-header validation implemented and tested (NFR-1R)

criteria.text: Workspace-based validation with honest statuses and offline Python/npm staging per ADR-007; unverified parts reported as limitations (FR-18)

criteria.text: C1 Real pip resolution, compatible and conflicting. Verified: `numpy==1.24.0`, `scipy==1.10.0`, `pandas==1.5.3` gives COMPATIBLE; `numpy==2.1.0` with `scipy==1.10.0` gives CONFLICT naming `scipy 1.10.0 depends on numpy<1.27.0` Evidence: `tests/test_resolution_live.py::test_numpy_scipy_compatible` and `::test_numpy_scipy_conflict`. Type: Integration. Docker: Yes.

C2 Transitive dependencies, markers, extras, constraints, `Requires-Python`. Verified: Transitive packages reported and verified; a marker-excluded dependency is absent; extras' dependencies present; a repository constraints file changes the outcome; a `Requires-Python` conflict gives CONFLICT; a transitive conflict between two direct dependencies is detected Evidence: `test_resolution_live.py::test_transitive`, `::test_markers`, `::test_extras`, `::test_constraints_file`, `::test_requires_python_conflict`, `::test_transitive_conflict`; supervisor closure unit tests on captured real reports (`tests/test_resolution_verifier.py`). Type: Integration + unit. Docker: Live: yes; unit: no.

C3 Prerelease and yanked policy. Verified: No prerelease unless pinned; a pinned prerelease is allowed; a yanked `==` pin resolves with a warning; yanked releases are not chosen for ranges Evidence: `test_resolution_live.py::test_prerelease_policy`, `::test_yanked_pin_warning`; unit tests on captured reports. Type: Integration + unit. Docker: Live: yes.

C4 Source-build handling. Verified: An sdist-only requirement (e.g. `pycrypto==2.6.1`) gives UNSUPPORTED `source_build_required`, never CONFLICT or COMPATIBLE; pip runs with `--only-binary=:all:`; no build backend runs (pip stderr has no build steps; the input mount stays unmodified); a conflict involving source-only releases gives UNSUPPORTED Evidence: `test_resolution_live.py::test_source_only_unsupported`; `tests/test_resolution_input.py`, `test_resolver_runtime.py::test_pip_args_binary_only`. Type: Integration + unit + security. Docker: Live: yes.

C5 Structured report and server-computed fingerprint. Verified: All report fields present; the fingerprint is computed by the supervisor; resolver stdout cannot set the status or fingerprint; **forgery tests:** a report claiming an unsatisfied `Requires-Dist` closure, wrong hashes, a non-allow-listed artifact host, extra packages, malformed JSON or excess size each give RESOLUTION_FAILED Evidence: `tests/test_resolution_verifier.py` (forgery matrix on captured real reports); `tests/test_resolution_fingerprint.py`. Type: Unit + security. Docker: No.
criteria.proof: tests/test_resolution_verifier.py (forgery matrix on captured real pip reports: injected status/fingerprint/role fields, unsatisfied Requires-Dist closure incl. forged success for numpy 2.1.0 + scipy 1.10.0, wrong hashes, non-allow-listed host, extra packages, malformed JSON, oversized report -> RESOLUTION_FAILED; all FR-27b fields; supervisor-computed fingerprint) and tests/test_resolution_fingerprint.py: passed locally (1091 passed) and in CI run 43273960784 on 0cf5e4d (Python 3.10-3.14). Unit + security; Docker not required.

criteria.text: C6 Input-change invalidation. Verified: Changing the proposal diff, original or proposed manifest, constraints, image digest, pip policy arguments or allow-list version changes the fingerprint; stored evidence then counts as UNKNOWN and approval is blocked Evidence: `test_resolution_fingerprint.py` (one case per input); `tests/test_resolution_enforcement.py::test_stale_evidence_blocks`. Type: Unit + API. Docker: No.

C7 Fail-closed enforcement. Verified: 6 statuses × {approve, validate, apply, export}: only COMPATIBLE with a matching fingerprint passes; client-supplied status or fingerprint fields are ignored; pre-M12 plans are UNKNOWN and blocked; M11 validation-policy enforcement is unchanged; npm plans are UNSUPPORTED and blocked Evidence: `tests/test_resolution_enforcement.py` (matrix), existing M11 suites. Type: API + security. Docker: No.

C8 Egress isolation in the real Docker setup. Verified: From inside a resolver container built by the production runtime: direct TCP to a public IP fails; DNS lookup fails; `CONNECT` to a non-allow-listed host is refused and logged; `CONNECT` to 169.254.169.254, the Docker gateway, the host IP and an RFC 1918 address is refused; `CONNECT pypi.org:22` is refused; plain HTTP is refused; `CONNECT pypi.org:443` succeeds; the proxy is not reachable from a container on another network. Proxy unit tests: rebinding (the validated IP is used), allow-list, ports, methods, denial log format Evidence: `tests/test_egress_live.py` (Docker), `tests/test_egress_proxy.py` (unit). Type: Security integration + unit. Docker: Live: yes.

C9 Resource limits and timeout. Verified: Generated `docker run` arguments include non-root, read-only, capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, `--init`, memory, CPU, processes, tmpfs size, read-only input mount, no writable host mount, no socket, internal network only, DNS disabled; timeout hierarchy (ADR-012): a run exceeding T gives TIMED_OUT and RESOLUTION_FAILED (`timeout`), with containers killed at the run deadline and no evidence for that run; a run-1 timeout prevents run 2; the job's terminal state is recorded by `started_at + 2T`; supervisor requests are bounded by the remaining run time; cleanup finishes within 30 s or the sweep removes leftovers; limit settings outside their ceilings are refused at startup Evidence: `tests/test_resolver_runtime.py` (args), `tests/test_resolution_config.py` (ceilings), `test_resolution_live.py::test_timeout_kills_containers`, `tests/test_job_service.py::test_timeout_hierarchy` (fake clock: run deadline, job deadline, run-2 budget shortened by slow setup). Type: Unit + integration. Docker: Live: yes.

C10 SQLite job lifecycle, cancellation and restart recovery. Verified: Two runs per job (original, then proposed), each with its own NFR-13 limits; cancel or timeout during either run stores no evidence for that run. Each state transition, with concurrent-transition rejection (compare-and-set); one active job per plan; pool bound; cancel: a QUEUED job is cancelled at once; a RUNNING job's watcher (≤ 1 s) kills the current container, skips the remaining run and records CANCELLED within 5 s, and removes the network; evidence is stored only for completed runs (an original row may remain, a proposed row never without SUCCEEDED); INTERRUPTED after a simulated restart with no evidence stored; startup sweep removes labelled leftovers but never a concurrently active job's resources; retention cascade Evidence: `tests/test_job_service.py` (unit, fake runner), `test_resolution_live.py::test_cancel_cleans_up`, `::test_restart_sweep`. Type: Unit + integration. Docker: Live: yes.

C11 Minimal UI integration. Verified: Compatibility panel states (checking, compatible, conflict, unsupported, failed, unavailable, unknown); cancel works; approval disabled with the reason; npm "not yet supported" message; no redesign Evidence: `frontend/src/components/*.test.tsx`; headless-Chrome journey (RESOLVER_UNAVAILABLE path locally; COMPATIBLE path requires Docker). Type: Component + end-to-end. Docker: E2E COMPATIBLE: yes.

C12 CI Docker integration. Verified: The CI Docker job runs `test_resolution_live.py` and `test_egress_live.py` with `DUA_REQUIRE_DOCKER=1` on the M12 commit; all jobs green Evidence: GitHub Actions run on the M12 commit. Type: CI. Docker: Yes.

C13 Documentation and backward compatibility. Verified: Revision 4 requirements, architecture, threat model and ADR-009 to ADR-012 match the implementation; supported and unsupported cases documented; pre-M12 records intact and UNKNOWN; additive migration tested on an M11-era database Evidence: `tests/test_resolution_migration.py`; `validate_artifacts.py`; reviewer check. Type: Unit + doc. Docker: No.

C14 Compatibility disclosure and resolved-set review (FR-32). Verified: (a) Every COMPATIBLE view and the Markdown export carry the disclosure "resolves, not vetted or safe; DUA does not perform malware detection", and no UI or export text claims safety. (b) A job runs the original then the proposed resolution under identical settings, storing separate evidence and fingerprints; introduced packages are exactly proposed set minus original set; when the original is not COMPATIBLE the comparison shows `comparison unavailable` with that status and nothing is flagged; the comparison never changes approval. (c) Upload date is the selected file's time matched by filename and SHA-256 (PEP 700 `upload-time`, else JSON API `upload_time_iso_8601`); source and retrieval time recorded; an unmatched file or missing time shows `date unavailable`; a multi-file version uses the selected file's time. (d) The complete list (name, version, direct or transitive, introduced, date) is in the UI and the export. Evidence: `tests/test_resolution_comparison.py` (set difference, unavailable cases, approval unaffected); `tests/test_upload_dates.py` (multi-file selection, PEP 700 and JSON API sources, no match, missing field, no fallback to other files); `tests/test_export_resolution.py`; component tests; `test_resolution_live.py::test_original_and_proposed_runs` (e.g. scipy upgrade introducing a new transitive package). Type: Unit + API + component + integration. Docker: Live: yes.

notes.text: Enabling strict approvals mode for Tier 3 project governance as requested by human user
M4 post-acceptance security hardening: atomic proposal consumption and concurrency-safe lifecycle states (AVAILABLE, APPLYING, CONSUMED).

M5 post-acceptance security remediation completed: workspace boundary validation, server-enforced network isolation, pinned image digests, bounded streaming log capture, explicit test discovery, and live CI container runner.

G1-approved MUST requirements not delivered by the 2.0 stack and neither scheduled nor deferred in the G3 plan: FR-1 (repository acquisition; legacy Streamlit only, no API/UI), FR-2 (recursive multi-manifest discovery; legacy only), FR-5 (AST inspection; legacy only), FR-7 (Monaco hunk review; unified diff only), FR-12 (SSE progress; absent), FR-13 (persistent history; tables unused). NFR-1 Host-header validation not implemented. NFR-7 test count (146) stale; current baseline 564 passed / 6 skipped. Requirements 'out of scope: npm' contradicts delivered npm support. Identified in engineering takeover 2026-11-11; to be resolved in Inception round 2.

Trust-boundary defects in the 2.0 baseline: client-supplied validation_status accepted by upgrade_planner (TRUSTED_VALIDATION_STATUSES); approval is a client-side boolean (isApproved) and /plan/apply is never called by the UI; export is not gated on approval; validation route does not pass source_workspace so sandbox validation is syntax-only; dependency_staging is a stub returning NOT_REQUIRED; registry_client 2 MB response cap fails large packages (e.g. numpy). Owner decision: baseline is not production-ready.

Correction to v2.0 completion report (Security review): Origin validation, Content-Type enforcement and X-DUA-Client anti-CSRF header checks (NFR-1, T-2) are NOT implemented in src/; only CORSMiddleware exists (src/api/main.py). The report's 'verified by tests' claim for these was wrong. To be implemented and tested in M10 together with Host-header validation.

M10 post-submission audit (2026-11-12, before commit): added unit-test guard against live package downloads, live Docker staging integration tests (tests/test_docker_staging_integration.py) wired into CI with DUA_REQUIRE_DOCKER=1, frontend CI job, UI marking of offline-catalog and failed registry lookups, quiet git clone. M10 remains awaiting human G4 approval.

Post-M10 hardening (2026-11-12, owner-directed, outside an approved milestone; uncommitted): fixed origin allow-list (Vite 5174 blocked); fixed host-side SSRF/dependency-confusion in staging (pip options and direct URLs in untrusted requirements; npm overrides/lockfile foreign hosts); plans persisted in SQLite with PLAN_RETENTION_HOURS and consumed-state replay protection; request IDs and non-leaking 500s; digest pinning fails closed. Recommend registering this as M11 via 'milestone add --replan' (requires G3 re-approval) before G5.
